figures.alt: White plumbing vent passing through shingles with a clean black pipe boot and flashing flange
figures.caption: A pipe boot is a small roof detail with a big job: it has to shed water around a moving roof penetration without interrupting the shingle courses above it.
figures.before: When You Need a Permit in Jacksonville

figures.alt: Metal roof drip edge and underlayment layered with asphalt shingles at an eave
figures.caption: The same overlap logic applies across the roof. A new boot belongs in an intact water-shedding sequence, not on top of weak shingles or compromised decking.

figures.alt: Finished curb-mounted skylight flashing integrated with an asphalt-shingle roof
figures.caption: If multiple roof penetrations show failed sealant, brittle shingles, or staining, it is worth evaluating the broader roof condition instead of replacing isolated parts one at a time.
